A recent subverse request for /v/science and the ensuing discussion about the role of moderators in dealing with posts/comments raised the issue of spam--link to the relevant part of the conversation. (NB: This link cuts off the preceding comments in the thread. Please view the entire comment thread for full context. I'm only linking to the middle for convenience.)

As per the Voat User Agreement, spam is prohibited in the global rule:

You may not post any graphics, text, photographs, images, video, audio or other material that we deem to be junk or spam.

The standard of "we deem," presumably referring to Atko and Puttitout, is opaque to the rest of us. Commonly, spam refers to messages sent to a large audience for purposes of advertising or malice. This certainly fits with a couple of posts I myself have removed. However in the aforementioned moderation discussion there's a suggestion of other content which is up for consideration as spam. The content is unwelcome and typically irrelevant to the subverse and/or post, yet does not necessarily feature links used for advertisement or distribution of malware. Moderators may feel justified in removing such content but that action ought to be clearly defined as either in the service of the site (actual "junk or spam," per User Agreement) or service of the moderator's preferences for the subverse.

May I request added clarity on what sort of content falls under the "junk or spam" provision of the User Agreement? Does the provision extend beyond promotional/malicious content? Is the standard based on the relevance of content to the subverse and/or post? Is a pattern of behavior across the subverse or site applicable to this determination? Or, ultimately, is this global rule enforced at the discretion of admins and mods?
A clarification on the site-wide definition of spam?

Spam is the intentional posting of any form of content that doesn't fit within the general topic of X subverse. That's how I see it an that's how most sites utilize anti-spam measures.

The main issue with it involves personal views of an individual. A political cartoon is a picture, it could possible be considered funny, and it's definitely considered political.

That means there are multiple baskets you can put it in and it's up to whomever mods each sub to decide if it belongs in that subverse based on that.

The moderation discussion you referred to was an attempt to classify harassment or bullying as spam, and I don't agree at all with this philosophy that this is Spam (unless it become repetitious, then delete away).

Spam is repetitious posts/comments plus advertising of any kind for a product or service or for an off-site blog or site.

It's not Spam of it's off topic to a subverse, that could simply be an error of submission, but it's still fair game for deletion if it doesn't meet the sub's theme. I also use the following on occasion to delete Spam, from the site's FAQ's:

Can I submit links to sites I operate?: Submitting only links to sites you operate (or are associated with), without submitting other, unrelated links, is considered spamming. If you submit niche content (for example gaming videos from your own YouTube channel), you should create your own subverse and submit the content only to that subverse. If majority of the links you submit are to sites you are associated with, your domains may be globally banned from Voat. To be on the safe side, if you submit 10 links to various subverses on Voat, at most 2 of the 10 submitted links may be to the sites you are associated with.
